messages:
mike: quick heads-up — ran a focused microbench across AWS/GCP/Azure for the A100-80GB SKU (driver 525.60, CUDA 11.8) against the llama-13b-qat runtime. results are odd: gcp shows ~8-12% higher token latency, azure has throughput variance under sustained load. full notes + commands below.

anya: can you paste the exact command + node setup?

devon: did we pin kernel and nv_peer_mem? gcp often ships different power governor defaults.

mike: command i used:
```
./bench-tool run --model=llama-13b-qat --gpu-type=A100-80GB --driver=525.60 --cuda=11.8 --batch=32 --seq=1024 --iters=300 --mode=throughput --pin-kernel 5.15.0-101
```
node setup: ubuntu 22.04, nvidia-driver=525.60, cuBLAS 11.8.0, MIG disabled, nv_peer_mem NOT loaded for baseline. collected nsys + ncu traces.

ci-bench-bot: artifact uploaded: https://ci.internal/reports/1778456789 (csv + perf traces) :white_check_mark:

rachel: quick summary (median of 3 runs):
- aws (us-west-2): avg token latency 36.5 ms, throughput ~= 880 tok/s
- gcp (us-central1): avg token latency 39.8 ms (+9%), throughput ~= 800 tok/s
- azure (westus2): avg token latency 37.2 ms, throughput ~= 780 tok/s, but 95th pct spikes at +30% under long runs

anya: do we know cuBLAS/cuDNN micro-version diffs across images? that can change kernel selection heuristics.

devon: dug into traces: gcp shows an extra ~1.0-1.8ms per token attributable to small memcpy H2D calls in the kernel timeline. azure shows more frequent kernel re-launches (maybe clock throttling).

mike: hypothesis: (a) small H2D latency due to host PCIe config or driver memcopy path, (b) azure host power/profile causing SM clocks to throttle under thermal/power constraints. plan: rerun with driver 525.85 everywhere, enable nv_peer_mem, and collect ncu on one run each.

anya: i'll take gcp + azure with 525.85 tomorrow morning. i'll also snapshot cuBLAS/cuDNN versions before/after.

rachel: i'll take aws and enable nv_peer_mem; will also test with MIG toggled on/off.

ci-bench-bot: scheduled jobs created: #1778456789-azure-52585, #1778456789-gcp-52585, #1778456789-aws-52585. expected ETA ~24h.

mike: if gaps persist after identical driver/CUDA, escalate to cloud infra to check BIOS PCIe gen and host firmware. thanks — please drop the ncu flamegraphs in the artifact. :eyes:
